clue.text: Feeble question repeated about divided tax-free accounts

indicators.note: each copy of the question word goes round one half of the split accounts

parts.note: why is a question word
ISAs are UK tax-free savings accounts; divided, the plural splits into IS and AS

indicators.note: the question-round-accounts construction is done a second time with the other half

parts.note: why is a question word
ISAs are UK tax-free savings accounts; divided, the plural splits into IS and AS

explanation.surface: Someone weakly keeps asking about splitting up their tax-free savings.
explanation.walkthrough: ISAs are British tax-free savings accounts; 'divided' splits the plural in two, and 'repeated' builds the second half the same way as the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Something insipid or lacking firmness is described with this reduplicated colloquial word for weak.

clue.text: Unintentionally showed live TV, only half ready to be broadcast

parts.note: to be is to live or exist

indicators.note: just the first of the two letters of the abbreviation is kept
broadcast as scattered, so the letters of the word ready are strewn about

explanation.surface: Someone accidentally aired a live television show before it was ready.
explanation.walkthrough: 'only half' keeps T of TV; 'to be broadcast' turns READY into RAYED.
explanation.definitionFit: To give away a feeling or secret without meaning to is a standard sense of the verb.

clue.text: Therapeutic movement that could make him curtsey

indicators.note: the letters of him and curtsey could be rearranged to form something new

explanation.surface: A gentle exercise routine so graceful that it might get a man to curtsey.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a system of rhythmic bodily movement to music, used in education and therapy.

clue.text: Slippery character missing a month's work

indicators.note: the abbreviated month is lost from the slippery creature's name

parts.note: an octopus is a slimy, slippery sea creature
Oct is the abbreviation for October

explanation.surface: A slippery colleague skips a month's worth of work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slippery character' looks like a crook; it is a sea creature, OCTOPUS, minus OCT.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for work, used for a numbered musical or literary composition.

clue.text: Corrected last section of paper in a day

indicators.note: the final letter of paper sits inside the abbreviated day

parts.note: Tue is the abbreviation for Tuesday

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word paper is taken

explanation.surface: The final part of a newspaper was put right within a single day.
explanation.definitionFit: Something accurate or set straight is described as right, exact or correct.

clue.text: Singer/songwriter's place in annex

indicators.note: the abbreviation for place goes inside the verb meaning annex

parts.note: to annex is to attach or join on
Pl is the address abbreviation for Place

explanation.surface: A musician's home is in an extension added onto a house.
explanation.definitionFit: Janis, the 1960s rock singer, and Scott, the ragtime composer, both bore this surname.

clue.text: Succeeded to get barrel underneath foor

indicators.note: in a down entry the barrel word is placed below the abbreviation
this word only joins the neighbouring pieces: it says which one stands next to which in the answer

parts.note: s is the abbreviation for succeeded in family trees
a tun is a large cask or barrel

explanation.surface: Someone succeeded in getting a barrel beneath the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue as held has the typo 'foor' for 'floor', the definition. 'underneath' puts TUN below S in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: To knock someone down or daze them flat is to floor them, just as a heavy blow does.

clue.text: At heart, girl is an auxiliary

indicators.note: only the central part of the word for a girl is kept, its ends shed

parts.note: a maiden is a girl or young unmarried woman

explanation.surface: Deep down, a young woman is a helper.
explanation.definitionFit: An assistant or helper, especially to a politician or officer, is an auxiliary.

clue.text: Introducing bible to populate devilish old country

indicators.note: the bible abbreviation is introduced into the shuffled letters
devilish suggests wild mischief, so the letters of populate are scrambled

parts.note: RV is the Revised Version of the Bible

explanation.surface: Missionaries bring the Bible to people a wicked place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'devilish' scrambles POPULATE to UPPEOLTA, and 'Introducing' sets the Bible abbreviation into those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The West African state was renamed Burkina Faso in 1984, so it is a former country name.

clue.text: King on grand carriage abroad

indicators.note: the king's name comes after the abbreviation for grand

parts.note: G is short for grand, a thousand pounds
Harry is a name borne by English kings such as Henry V

explanation.surface: A monarch rides in a stately vehicle overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse-drawn cab used in India and Egypt, hence a carriage found abroad.

clue.text: Straight line separating smooth sort of sheep

indicators.note: the heterosexual and line pieces split the smoothing word in two

parts.note: to sand is to smooth with abrasive paper
het is slang for heterosexual, i.e. straight

explanation.surface: A dead straight line divides the smoothed fleece of a breed of sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: A small hardy breed from the Scottish northern isles is named after them.

clue.text: Departed by main route?

parts.note: A is first-class or principal, as in British A-roads, the main routes
a way is a route or road

explanation.surface: Someone left by travelling along the main road.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has gone off or left is said to be gone, not here.

clue.text: Heavy blow given by drunk regimental soldier

indicators.note: the blow piece follows the drunk piece, which gives it its place

parts.note: high means intoxicated
a lander is a heavy punch or blow, from landing one

explanation.surface: A hard punch thrown by a drunkard.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of Scottish infantry regiments such as the Gordon or Seaforth are so called.

clue.text: Finally building hospital east of banana republic

indicators.note: the final letter of building is taken

parts.note: H is the map abbreviation for hospital

indicators.note: only the eastern, right-hand end of the word banana is kept, its first three letters shed

explanation.surface: A hospital is at last built to the east of a corrupt little state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banana republic' reads as one phrase, but only 'republic' defines; 'east of' keeps the right-hand end of BANANA, dropping BAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The West African nation became a republic in 1960, after the Gold Coast won independence.

clue.text: Wife feeding insecure, threatening character old stews

indicators.note: the abbreviation for wife is fed in between the two other pieces

parts.note: loose means not firmly fixed, insecure
an omen is a portent with an ominous character

explanation.surface: A wife feeds an unstable, menacing figure on old casseroles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stews' looks like casseroles; in old usage a stew was a brothel or a prostitute.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaic slang called prostitutes stews, after the bathhouses doubling as brothels.

clue.text: Unpredictable mover and shaker

parts.note: a mover and shaker is usually an influential person, but here it is the ground literally shifting and shaking without warning

explanation.definitionFit: A seismic tremor moves and shakes the ground and cannot be forecast.

clue.text: Reviled sailor no longer employed

indicators.note: the sailor is dropped from the word for reviled

parts.note: abused means insulted or reviled
AB is an able-bodied seaman

explanation.surface: An insulted sailor has lost his job.
explanation.definitionFit: Something put to use or made use of has been utilised.

clue.text: State of a female prostitute

parts.note: Ida is a woman's name
ho is slang for a prostitute

explanation.surface: A remark about the condition of a woman who sells sex.
explanation.definitionFit: A US state in the Pacific Northwest, famous for potatoes.

clue.text: Redundancy means "go into retirement", only initially

indicators.note: the opening letter of each of go, into, retirement and only is taken

explanation.surface: Being laid off means you must simply retire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'only' reads as a qualifier on 'initially' but its O is the last letter picked.
explanation.definitionFit: A British state benefit cheque, the payment given to someone out of work.

clue.text: Where you might enter (with pen) bent item in book?

parts.note: a gate is an entrance to a field or garden
a fold is a pen for sheep

explanation.surface: A form asks where to write, in pen, the title of a damaged book.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide page folded in on itself to fit a book or magazine is bent over.

clue.text: Scrape by, blessed by church network that links all

indicators.note: blessed used like a mild curse, signalling the letters are messed up

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A poor parish gets by, blessed by a church that links its whole community.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blessed' makes CYBERSPA from SCRAPE BY; the second 'by' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: The notional online realm of computer networks connecting everyone.

clue.text: Abandon former attitude

parts.note: ex means former
a pose is a bodily attitude or posture

explanation.surface: Give up the way you used to carry yourself.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave an infant out in the open to die is an old sense of the verb, abandonment.

clue.text: Some Wiltshire dialect used in 14

indicators.note: only some of the letters of Wiltshire are used, a run inside it

explanation.surface: A bit of West Country dialect turns up in Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Twi, also spelt this way, is an Akan language spoken in the West African country at 14.

clue.text: Blocked a unit with heavy-duty fencing

indicators.note: the heavy-duty abbreviation fences in, or surrounds, the unit

parts.note: HD is short for heavy-duty
the ampere is the SI unit of electric current

explanation.surface: Access was obstructed by strong fencing around a unit.
explanation.definitionFit: To be hindered or impeded in movement is to be obstructed.

clue.text: Host with many branches?

definitions.meaning: a host is a great multitude, especially an armed force
jokingly, having many arms, like a tree with many limbs

explanation.definitionFit: A host is an army in old usage, and arm plus y reads as having many arms.

clue.text: Unlimited group sex — at last, something saucy

indicators.note: the outer letters of group are removed, leaving its middle
the final letter of sex is used

explanation.surface: Unrestrained group sex is, at last, something racy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saucy' suggests racy, but it means sauce-making.
explanation.definitionFit: A cooked mixture of butter and flour forms the base of many sauces.

clue.text: Old explorer, one in endless bewilderment

indicators.note: the numeral for one goes inside the shortened word for bewilderment
the final letter of the word for bewilderment is cut off

parts.note: a daze is a state of bewilderment
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An early explorer, one forever confused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts DAZE to DAZ, around I.
explanation.definitionFit: Bartolomeu, the Portuguese navigator who rounded the Cape of Good Hope in 1488, bore this name.

clue.text: Waste away, wounded

parts.note: off means away, as in going off
cut means wounded by a blade

explanation.surface: Someone is wasting away after being injured.
explanation.definitionFit: A leftover scrap trimmed from material is discarded refuse.

clue.text: Delayed by us, came undone missing tackle?

indicators.note: the delayed word is set beside, after, the shuffled letters
undone means unravelled, so the letters of us and came are rearranged

parts.note: late means delayed

explanation.surface: Held up by us, someone arrived dishevelled and missing their fishing gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'undone' makes EMASCU from US CAME. 'tackle' looks like fishing gear; it is slang for male genitals.
explanation.definitionFit: As an old adjective, deprived of male genitals, i.e. castrated, slangily lacking the tackle.

clue.text: Mere holiday up north

definitions.meaning: a mere is a pond or small body of water
in northern English dialect, to laik or ... is to play or take time off work

explanation.definitionFit: A mere is a stretch of still water, and in Northern dialect the word also means to play.
